+def _log_function(logger: _Logger | None) -> Callable[[str, int], None] | None:
+    """
+    Turn the ``logger`` argument of :py:func:`exif_transpose` into one function that
+    takes a message and a :py:mod:`logging` level, or ``None`` if there is no logger.

+    A standard logger receives the message at that level. Any other callable is
+    called with the message alone. An object that only has methods named like the
+    levels (``info``, ``warning``) is accepted too.
+    """
+    if logger is None:
+        return None
+    if isinstance(logger, (logging.Logger, logging.LoggerAdapter)):
+        return lambda message, level: logger.log(level, message)
+    if callable(logger):
+        return lambda message, level: logger(message)
+
+    method_names = {logging.INFO: "info", logging.WARNING: "warning"}
+
+    def log_with_method(message: str, level: int) -> None:
+        getattr(logger, method_names[level])(message)
+
+    if all(callable(getattr(logger, name, None)) for name in method_names.values()):
+        return log_with_method
+    msg = "logger must be callable or a logging.Logger"
+    raise TypeError(msg)
+
